title: Live-cell assay to detect the dynamics of protein interactions
protocol: Mix plasmid vectors in sterile electroporation cuvettes.
Add empty vector DNA to maintain constant total amount of DNA for each experiment.
Rinse cell monolayer with phosphate buffered saline.
Treat cells briefly with trypsin (0.05%) containing 0.53 mM EDTA.
Remove trypsin-EDTA solution.
Resuspend cells in culture medium containing serum when they begin to release from the flask surface.
Wash cells twice by centrifugation in Dulbecco’s calcium-magnesium free phosphate buffered saline.
Resuspend cells to a concentration of approximately 1x10^7 cells per ml in Dulbecco’s calcium-magnesium free phosphate buffered saline.
Add 400 μl of cell suspension to each 0.2 cm gap electroporation cuvette containing the DNA.
Gently mix contents of the cuvette.
Pulse cells at a desired voltage and capacitance.
Use a 220 volt pulse with a total capacitance of 1200 microfarads for GHFT1-5 cells in 400 μl suspension in 0.2 cm gap cuvettes.
Recover cells from the cuvette.
Dilute cells in phenol red free tissue culture medium containing serum.
Inoculate cells drop-wise onto a sterile 42-mm cover glass in 60 mm culture dishes.
Allow cells to attach to the cover glass for approximately 20 minutes.
Gently flood the culture dish with media.
Place cultures in an incubator for 18 hours prior to imaging.
Prepare chambers for cell attachment.
Cut stainless steel to external dimensions of 74 x 65 mm and create a circular chamber with a diameter of 50 mm and depth of 4.5 mm.
Drill the center portion of the chamber to support a 42-mm cover glass.
Polish surfaces of the chamber and insert for a tight seal against the cover glass.
Place cover glass with monolayer of transfected cells in the chamber.
Tighten the insert snuggly to the glass.
Fill the chamber with media.
Fit the chamber to the prewarmed stage of the inverted microscope.
Cover the chamber with the top from a 60 mm dish.
Maintain temperature between 35-37°C using a stage incubator.
Use culture medium buffered for room air conditions if cultures are exposed to it.
Co-transfect cells with mRFP marker for visualization under arc lamp illumination.
Identify transfected cells using epi-fluorescence microscopy configuration.
Identify a transfected cell by mRFP fluorescence using the Texas Red filter.
Switch to LSM mode.
Acquire a focused image of the selected cell using the red channel only.
Crop the image to the size of the cell using the Crop function.
Set the maximum scanning speed possible for the selected zoom factor.
Adjust the gain and laser power so that the brightest pixel in the 8-bit image is between 200 and 250 gray levels, guided by the Histogram function.
Open a new image window.
Turn on the green channel.
Do a preliminary scan of the cell.
Set the number of scans and delay between scans under the Time Lapse function.
Optimize the delay for individual PA-GFP-labeled proteins, setting it to zero for high mobility proteins.
Under the Edit Bleach function, set the activation pulse length and intensity.
Start with 15 iterations and 405-nm laser at 100% transmittance.
Define the number of images before the activation pulse.
Choose and draw a circular activation ROI under the Define ROI function.
Use a 20 pixel-diameter ROI to minimize photodamage.
Save the selected ROI for future experiments.
Place the photoactivation ROI in the area of the cell where PA-GFP is to be activated.
Return to the Time Lapse window and press Start Bleach.
Review the image sequence by choosing the _Slice_ function.
Determine the change in fluorescence intensity over time in several user-defined regions of interest (ROIs) using the _Profile_ function.
Display and save actual intensity values for each selected ROI using the _Show Table_ function.
Repeat steps 16-19 with different cells until the photoactivation pulse is optimized.
Identify transfected cells that co-express PA-GFP- and CFP-labeled proteins by fluorescence in the cyan channel using the visible (VIS) mode with the FITC filter.
Switch back to the LSM mode.
Turn off the red and cyan channels.
Focus and crop the selected cell using the 488-nm laser line.
Acquire the "before photoactivation" GFP image.
Turn off the green channel.
Turn on the cyan channel (ex 405 nm/em 475 nm).
Take a preliminary image in a new window.
Adjust the detector gain so the brightest pixel is between 200 and 250 gray levels.
Acquire the "before photoactivation" CFP image.
Position the photoactivation ROI that was saved from the previous set of experiments.
Use the optimized photoactivation protocol described in steps 16-19.
Collect images with the 405-nm laser line at 1.5 μW laser power at the frequency determined as described above.
Open a new image window.
Turn off the cyan channel.
Turn on the green channel to acquire the "after photoactivation" GFP image under identical conditions to the first.
Repeat the data analysis described in step 10 using the cyan image sequence.
Analyze the change in the cyan signal in different ROI positioned at different distances from the activation site.
Repeat steps 21 to 24 with cells that are transfected with the CFP construct only.
Repeat steps 21 to 25 with cells that are transfected with the CFP-labeled protein of interest and a PA-GFP-labeled protein that does not interact with the protein of interest.
Open saved tables in Microsoft Excel.
For each ROI, normalize data to the initial fluorescence by dividing all values by the first value in the column.
Normalize GFP-alone data so the highest value equals 1.
Measure change in CFP intensity over time for several different ROIs.
Normalize measured CFP intensity changes to the initial fluorescence in each ROI.
Plot data as relative intensity versus time.
